meta_desc: How bridge42worlds works from the inside: architecture, economics, plans — and an invitation to the supervisory board.
og_desc: The project's architecture, economics, and plans — and an invitation for those who read to the end.
hero_eyebrow: for those who read to the end
hero_dek: You have opened enough articles for this text to interest you. Here, without a display window: architecture, money, what is broken, what lies ahead — and an invitation to truly participate.
why_h2: Science gets published faster than it can be explained
why_lead: More than two thousand papers are posted on arXiv every day. They are written by scientists for scientists, and a person without a physics degree cannot get in — not because they wouldn't understand the idea, but because they can't get through the language.
why_body: We translate fresh science into plain human language — every day, in five languages. We don't retell science news: we take the actual paper, read it in full, and write it so that anyone interested can understand. The same article — at four levels of depth, from 'the gist in ten seconds' to a breakdown with formulas and the history of the discovery.
why_th_2: What that means for the product
believe_1_b: We don't hide formulas; we explain them: each one has an author, a step-by-step derivation, and the meaning of every symbol
believe_2_b: All five languages are equal; Arabic is not a checkbox translation but a full version with the correct writing direction
believe_3_b: Above the articles lives a map: topics, laws, scientists, and the connections between them
believe_4_a: Readers are smarter than they're given credit for
believe_4_b: No baby talk or clickbait: interesting things are interesting on their own
believe_5_b: If an article hasn't been translated, it says so outright, rather than slipping in a text in another language
now_note: The numbers are pulled from the site when the page loads — if something else is shown above, the project has grown since this text was written.
row_full: — full, based on the full text of the work
row_express: — express, based on the author's abstract
row_refs_d: 369 topics, 145 laws, 201 scientists — all described and translated
row_search_d: cross-lingual: an Arabic query finds English articles
row_order_d: mechanism exists, funnel not built out
row_reuse_d: on upgrade we pay twice — the main technical debt
row_arxiv_d: so that any paper can be ordered for analysis
how_h2: The site is already built — all of it, entirely
how_p: Pages are not assembled when you open them: all forty-plus thousand lie as ready files in object storage. It’s a boring solution, but almost everything else follows from it.
how_1_b: Nothing to crash under load, hosting costs peanuts
how_2_a: The page is served from storage
how_2_b: Fast anywhere in the world, including the Gulf
how_3_b: Search, bot, and reactions are separate calls; the rest is static
how_4_b: One pass over the whole tree, about two hours
how_path: arXiv → selection → downloading PDF and extracting illustrations → generation of four depths in the source language → translation into four languages with verification of numbers, formulas, and markers → HTML assembly → publication.
how_check: Translation checking is not a formality. The validator verifies that all numbers from the source made it into the translation, that formulas are unchanged, and that entity labels are not lost; if something doesn’t match, the translation is redone. This is how cases where the model “improves” a study’s results are caught.
money_h2: The economics from which all decisions grow
money_p: This is not an abstraction: the price determines what we can afford, and almost every product decision is a consequence of this table.
money_2_c: based on the author's abstract, without PDF analysis
money_3_c: we use the illustration from the work itself, not create one
money_note: Current approach. Only express articles are produced on a daily basis — 20–25 a day, with a focus on natural sciences. The full article has become a luxury and is spent deliberately: at the reader's request and on works that deserve it.
poll_money_q: If the budget allows doing twice as much — where should it go?
poll_money_1: More full analyses instead of express articles
poll_money_2: More articles per day, even short ones
funnel_p: How a paper goes from raw publication to full analysis — and why this path is currently more expensive than it should be.
funnel_0_b: raw abstract → vector, search across arXiv
funnel_1_b: by abstract, immediately in all languages
funnel_2_b: across the full text, in the language of the query
funnel_note: What is broken and why it matters. The funnel rule: the express version must not vanish on upgrade — its text should become a short version of the full article, and its translations remain where the full version is not yet available. Currently the rule is broken: on upgrade everything is generated anew, and we pay for the same text twice. This is the project's main technical debt, and it is being worked on.
poll_funnel_q: Imagine: you find a paper on arXiv that we have not covered. What feels more natural to you?
poll_funnel_1: A “cover this paper” button and wait a couple of minutes
poll_funnel_2: A short summary immediately, full analysis on demand
poll_funnel_3: Leave a request and get an email when it is ready
next_h2: Plans — and what we are still debating
next_1_b: “experiment tables” instead of pictures: tweak a parameter and see what happens
next_2_b: question → search through our corpus → answer strictly based on what was found, with links; if it does not know, it says so
next_3_b: learn to find in the stream the works that in a year will be described as 'this is where it started'
next_4_b: the scheme was tested on French: first reference materials, then articles
next_5_b: titles as in science; this page is part of the concept
open_p: An honest list of what we have not agreed upon. If you have an opinion, it will be more useful to us than agreement.
open_1_a: How many full analyses per week are justified
open_1_b: depends on whether we learn to distinguish a breakthrough from merely good work
open_2_a: How to select scientific fields for expansion
open_2_b: currently the focus is on natural sciences, with mathematics and machine learning intentionally given less attention
open_3_a: Is monetization needed, and what kind
open_3_b: see the next section — we have a principle here, but no solution
poll_next_q: Which of the plans do you need most?
join_lead: Thank you for reading this far. If you've made it here, you've already done more than most: you've figured out how what you use works.
join_p: We invite you to the project's supervisory board. This is not an honorary certificate nor a scheduled job: it is the right to see how decisions are made and to speak up when you believe we are wrong.
rules_h3: Council rules — there are only three
rule_1_b: We do not sell access, do not show advertising, and do not trade on readers' attention.
rule_2_b: If the project ever starts receiving money, it goes to development: more analyses, more languages, better tools.
rule_3_b: Honestly, transparently, and fairly. If someone's work benefits the project, it should not remain unpaid by default.
rules_note: The third rule is our answer to the monetization question: we do not exclude it, but any form of it is checked against these three points and discussed with the council before it happens.
enter_p: We don't need registration — no password, no account. A name to address you by and an email to contact you are enough. You'll receive a key: with it you can always return and continue the conversation from the same point.
f_note: What you'd like to say — optional
f_note_ph: What you disagree with, what you would do differently, how you could help
key_note: Save the key. We'll recognize you by it even if you write from a different email. It lives in this browser and nowhere else until you submit the application.
honest: Your answers to the questions above are stored only in your browser. They are attached to the application if you decide to submit it — and go nowhere if you don't.
